configuration.build.title: Build & Log
configuration.codeblocks.build.asmUsesCo: For assembly files (.s/.asm/.ss/.s62) pick the compiler program via compilerVar (true = fully aligned with Code::Blocks: `.s` defaults to CPP, i.e. g++; false = keep the extension default of forcing the C compiler, which is safer for embedded scenarios)
configuration.codeblocks.build.cleanResp: Also delete the response files in the target object directory on Clean/Rebuild (*.respFile: temporary @file input generated for over-long commands; both linking and compiling can produce them). Code::Blocks never cleans up response files, so this is off by default to stay aligned; when enabled, Clean/Rebuild removes them too, so stale response files do not pile up forever (response files can always be deleted safely and are regenerated when needed)
configuration.codeblocks.build.compileCo: Whether a CommandsOnly target (type=4) compiles its files (aligned with Code::Blocks: CB compiles the files of a CommandsOnly target with empty options/empty includes; off by default to keep the extension's original behavior of running only the pre/post scripts)
configuration.codeblocks.build.compilerC: Off (default): no tool is probed and no prefix is injected; commands are exactly as before
Enable ccache: prefix standard compile commands with ccache (reuses objects by preprocessed result + options + toolchain hash; for GCC/Clang, choose sccache for MSVC)
Enable sccache: prefix standard compile commands with sccache (local disk cache, plus optional cloud backends)

Compiler cache (protective enhancement, off by default): when enabled, only **standard compile commands** are prefixed with `ccache`/`sccache` (linking/packing/resource compilation, pre/post scripts and `compile_commands.json` are not injected). The tool location is probed automatically (PATH → WinGet Links / WinGet Packages / Scoop shims / cargo bin / Chocolatey / Program Files) and can also be set explicitly via `#codeblocks.build.compilerCachePath#`; **when the tool is not found the build falls back to the original compiler** and logs one warning, without affecting the build result. When a tool is detected but not enabled, you are **asked once per workspace open** (with a "Don't ask again" option), and the detection result (version + path) is written to the output channel. Installation guide: run [Code::Blocks: Install Compiler Cache](command:codeblocks.installCompilerCache) from the Command Palette

Explicit path to the compiler cache tool executable (e.g. `C:\tools\ccache\ccache.exe`); empty = auto-detect (PATH → WinGet Links / WinGet Packages / Scoop shims / cargo bin / Chocolatey / Program Files). Only takes effect when [compiler cache](#codeblocks.build.compilerCache) is not `none`; **an invalid path counts as not found** (no silent fallback to PATH, so you never end up using an unintended cache program) and the build falls back to the original compiler
configuration.codeblocks.build.linkInput: Extensions of in-project link input files recognized by the incremental build (default `.xm` only; add `.ld`/`.lds` linker scripts, `.icf`, `.def`, etc. as needed): changing them relinks/repacks automatically (protective enhancement; Code::Blocks requires filling in External dependencies by hand). Accepts the `xm`/`.xm`/`*.xm` forms (case-insensitive; a comma/semicolon separated string also works, and an invalid value falls back to the default). Set to an empty array [] to disable this enhancement. Applies only to files not explicitly compiled (compile defaults to false); files with compile="1" are forced to relink on every build per CB's item counting rules
configuration.codeblocks.build.outputTim: Whether each line of the regular output channel carries a timestamp (off by default; when on, the format is 2026-09-29 15:11:20.222, the same as the log file). Takes effect only when persistLog is off (regular channel); changes apply immediately
configuration.codeblocks.build.persistLo: Persist the build output channel log (off by default): when enabled, output is written to a log file and history is kept across windows (CodeBlocks.log under %APPDATA%\Code\logs); when disabled, the regular output channel is used — history is cleared when the window reloads and can be cleared at any time with the "Code::Blocks: Clear Build Output" command. Reload the window for changes to take effect
configuration.codeblocks.build.plainCbLo: Plain Code::Blocks log mode: disables script numbering/the single-line completion style/the Emoji summary block/the slowest Top 3, and prints a CB-style === Build finished === line at the end of the build
configuration.codeblocks.build.profile.d: Build performance probe: appends a [profile] phase timing block to the Code::Blocks output channel after the build (environment preparation/collection (incremental decision · command generation)/first process latency/compilation/linking/host output parsing + spawn count and output volume), for performance diagnosis and before/after comparisons. Equivalent environment variable: CB_BUILD_PROFILE=1 (either one enables it; off by default with zero overhead and no behavior change)
configuration.codeblocks.build.responseF: Response file strategy for over-long commands: safe = the extension's protective default (threshold 8000, absolute path references, names keep the source extension as main.c.respFile); cb = aligned with Code::Blocks (threshold 32767, name main.respFile, relative path references)
configuration.codeblocks.build.saveHtmlL: Save an HTML build log when the build finishes (aligned with Code::Blocks' save_html_build_log, off by default): written as <project file name>_build_log.html (for workspace builds, <workspace file name>_build_log.html), containing the build start/end time plus a diagnostics summary table

Output the full command line in the HTML build log (aligned with Code::Blocks' save_html_build_log/full_command_line "Always output the full command line in the generated HTML file", off by default). Only takes effect when codeblocks.build.saveHtmlLog is on
configuration.codeblocks.build.scriptCom: Timeout for a single pre/post-build script command (milliseconds, default 0 = no timeout, matching Code::Blocks' infinite wait; upper limit 3600000). On timeout the whole process tree of that command is killed forcibly and the build is marked as failed; useful for long blocking scenarios such as reconnecting a network drive (SMB) inside a script or an upload service (.NET default 100s timeout). Applies to script commands only and does not affect compiling/linking
configuration.codeblocks.build.scriptExi: Exit grace period for pre/post-build script commands (milliseconds, default 1500, upper limit 60000). After the command itself (cmd.exe) exits, wait at most this long to drain trailing pipe output; if the pipe closes in the meantime, continue immediately. Code::Blocks waits for the command itself only → set to 0 for full alignment (background programs started with start/daemons in the script no longer slow down post-build); if the script really needs to wait for a background program to finish, use a foreground command or start /wait
configuration.codeblocks.build.skipInclu: Skip the #include dependency scan during incremental builds (aligned with Code::Blocks' skip_include_deps setting, for non-C/C++ compilers)
configuration.codeblocks.build.strictQuo: Strict quoting rules (aligned with Code::Blocks NeedQuotes: quote only for spaces); off by default for the loose rules (spaces + cmd metacharacters, preventing shell re-parsing)
configuration.codeblocks.build.verboseOu: Verbose build output: full compile command lines (aligned with Code::Blocks verbose mode), per-file lists for clean/rebuild, and the list of files skipped by the incremental build
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.buildLog: Diagnostics source for the Build Log view when clangd is detected: build = full diagnostics from the build engine (default, covering all compiled files); clangd = use clangd diagnostics (only files that have been opened, possibly incomplete). Either way the Problems panel is produced by clangd
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.builtinH: Value written to CompileFlags.BuiltinHeaders: clangd = use clangd's own builtin headers (default, the current behavior); queryDriver = builtin headers extracted from the cross compiler via --query-driver (stddef.h/stdarg.h etc. match the real toolchain; best combined with the two settings below)
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.clangTid: clang-tidy diagnostics: default = the key is not written (clangd's clang-tidy checks are on by default); off = writes Diagnostics.ClangTidy.Remove: ['*'] to disable all clang-tidy diagnostics (which are noisy in embedded code). To disable only a few checks, write   your own Remove list in extraConfig
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.completi: Value written to Completion.AllScopes (whether completion includes symbols from scopes that are not currently visible, adding the scope prefix automatically): default = the key is not written (clangd default is Yes); no = only suggest visible scopes (shorter completion list, less CPU); yes = explicitly on
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.document: Value written to Documentation.CommentFormat (how comments are parsed for documentation): default = the key is not written (clangd default is Plaintext, so markdown syntax is not rendered); doxygen = parse as Doxygen (hover adds parameter/return descriptions, recommended for projects that follow SDK comment conventions); markdown / plaintext can also be set explicitly
Whether to enable the clangd integration (generates compile_commands.json automatically and updates the clangd user configuration). Completion and go-to-definition only work once the clangd extension is installed
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.excludeD: Value written to If.PathExclude: files under these directory names (relative to the project tree, e.g. obj / bin / Debug) do not use this project's fragment. Empty by default (nothing excluded). Debug output directories usually have no analysis value, so excluding them cuts down pointless clangd work
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.extraCon: Free-form YAML appended to every project fragment (as a later fragment in the same scope it can override any key written by the extension, e.g. Diagnostics: MissingIncludes: Strict or Completion: ArgumentLists: Delimiters). The extension adds this project's scope If for it automatically, so you do not have to write If yourself. Note: a YAML syntax error makes clangd discard the entire config.yaml (including the extension fragment), so indent with spaces and do not write --- separator lines
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.forcedIn: Names of the base headers force-included when clangd analyzes header files (looked up in the include search paths; added with -include if found). Default is global.h (basic typedef/macro/sfr/clib context); do not use a master header such as include.h that includes all headers, or the headers it includes will be included recursively and produce many false positives
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.headerIn: Value written to Completion.HeaderInsertion (whether accepting a completion inserts the #include automatically): never = never insert (default, avoiding headers that do not exist in embedded projects); iwyu = clangd's default behavior (insert the owning header as needed); omit = the key is not written, leaving it to clangd's default or your own configuration
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.indexBac: Value written to Index.Background (background indexing): default = the key is not written (clangd default is build); skip = no background index for project files (cuts clangd's CPU/memory usage noticeably on large SDKs, at the cost of weaker cross-file navigation/find-references); build = explicitly on
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.indexSta: Value written to Index.StandardLibrary (whether to pre-index the standard library so std symbols complete in empty files): default = the key is not written (clangd default is on); false = off (saves memory for bare-metal/embedded projects without a standard library); true = explicitly on
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.inlayHin: Value written to InlayHints.Enabled (inline hints such as parameter names/inferred types): default = the key is not written (decided by clangd and the VS Code settings together); off = disable inlay hints (less clutter in the code area); on = enable
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.queryDri: Whether to prompt for/enable --query-driver when generating the configuration (so clangd queries the cross gcc directly for system headers and target information, instead of the extension's hand-written -isystem/--target workaround). Where it is written is chosen interactively by the codeblocks.clangd.applyQueryDriver command (workspace settings / user settings / copy to clipboard); this switch only affects the prompt and the documentation guidance
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.restartO: Whether to restart clangd when the active project switches and the compile database actually changed (because of shared files), so already open files are immediately re-analyzed with the new active project's compile command (refreshing squiggles/completion/navigation). The restart triggers re-indexing in clangd, so turn it off if it happens too often
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.suppress: Whether to suppress all diagnostics in header files (opening a .h file on its own no longer shows false positives such as unknown type name). SDK headers are generally not self-contained, so analyzing them alone always reports errors; real diagnostics in .c files are unaffected

Diagnostics suppressed in clangd diagnostics (written to Diagnostics.Suppress; accepts -W group names such as -Wunused-function or clangd diagnostic names such as redefinition_different_typedef). Two false positives commonly seen across embedded SDK boundaries are suppressed by default: a static function's compile-time assertion going unused, and typedef conflicts between SDK headers and toolchain system headers (__int32_t etc.); remove the corresponding entry to show it again
configuration.codeblocks.clangd.unusedIn: Value written to Diagnostics.UnusedIncludes (unused header hints): none = disable the hints (default, since embedded SDK headers include each other widely); strict = let clangd report unused #include directives; omit = the key is not written, leaving it to clangd's default or your own configuration (note that clangd 17+ defaults to strict)
configuration.codeblocks.compilerProgram: Full paths to the compiler programs. Grouped by compiler id (recommended): {"avr-gcc":{"C":"…\\avr-gcc.exe"}}; the old flat form {"C":"…"} only applies to the global compilerId it belongs to (the old behavior applied globally and leaked cross compiler programs into other families, which is now fixed). Cross compilers are written automatically by "Detect Compilers"; leave normal compilers empty to fall back to a PATH lookup.
configuration.codeblocks.debug.addOtherP: Add the directories of other open projects to the debug source search (aligned with Code::Blocks debugger settings' add other project search dirs; off by default)
configuration.codeblocks.debug.charset.d: Debug character set (GDB set charset, e.g. UTF-8 / GBK; empty = not set)
configuration.codeblocks.debug.disableIn: Pass -nx to GDB when starting a debug session, so user startup scripts (.gdbinit/gdb.ini) are not executed (aligned with Code::Blocks Debugger settings' Disable startup scripts (-nx); CB has it on by default). Turn this setting off if your local .gdbinit should take effect
configuration.codeblocks.debug.disassemb: Disassembly syntax flavor (GDB set disassembly-flavor); default = not set (follows the GDB default); custom = use the value of instructionSet
configuration.codeblocks.debug.gdbPath.d: Path to the GDB executable (empty = auto-detect: masterPath/bin → PATH). For cross-architecture toolchains it is best to point this at the matching gdb explicitly to avoid architecture mismatches
configuration.codeblocks.debug.initComma: GDB commands injected after the debug session starts (executed one by one on the CLI, e.g. set pagination off); aligned with Code::Blocks Debugger settings' initialization commands
configuration.codeblocks.debug.instructi: Custom disassembly flavor argument: used as the value of set disassembly-flavor only when disassemblyFlavor = custom (aligned with Code::Blocks' instruction set)
configuration.codeblocks.debug.printElem: Maximum number of elements shown for arrays/strings (GDB set print elements; 0 = not set, using the GDB default)
configuration.codeblocks.debug.printPret: Prettify the display of debug variables (GDB set print pretty on, structs indented over multiple lines)
configuration.codeblocks.debug.registers: The Registers view reads register values (off by default: some MinGW GDB 8.1 builds crash the GDB process while reading registers, which ends the debug session; enable it once you have confirmed your GDB does not have this problem)
configuration.codeblocks.debug.trace.des: Debug protocol tracing: writes DAP requests/responses/events to the Code::Blocks output channel (enable it when troubleshooting issues such as "session ends unexpectedly/breakpoints do not take effect")
configuration.codeblocks.debug.userArgum: Arguments appended to the GDB command line (quote-aware tokenization); aligned with Code::Blocks     Debugger settings' user arguments
configuration.codeblocks.detect.autoOpen: Workspace project auto-detection behavior: all / single / off. For a workspace whose parent directory holds many projects, single or off is recommended, so that a full workspace-level scan is not done on every window start
Show a multi-select when multiple projects are detected (protected by the autoOpenThreshold threshold, default)
Open automatically only when a single project is detected
Do not detect/open automatically (you can still detect manually from the status bar entry or the project management menu)

Auto-detection threshold (1–1000): when the number of unopened projects exceeds this value the multi-select is no longer shown automatically (only the status bar entry plus an output channel hint), and it also limits the number of projects restored for the session; this avoids the multiplied clangd/symbol indexing cost of "opening N projects at once"
configuration.codeblocks.editor.asmHashC: Comment marker for assembly files (`.s` / `.S`): off by default uses `//` (safe for preprocessed `.S`); when on, comment operations such as `Ctrl+/` use GAS's native `#` (required to assemble native `.s` directly — GAS rejects `//`). Changes apply immediately.
configuration.codeblocks.editor.autoHead: Automatically insert a header guard when a new empty header file (.h/.hpp/.hxx) is created (aligned with the headerguard plugin; files that already have a #pragma once / #ifndef guard are left alone)
configuration.codeblocks.editor.headerGu: How the header guard is inserted: `ifndef` = wrap with `#ifndef` / `#define` / `#endif` (default); `pragma-once` = only `#pragma once` at the top
configuration.codeblocks.editor.tidyComm: Wrap width for tidy comments (block comment cleanup), in columns
configuration.codeblocks.gdbTimeoutMs.de: GDB MI command timeout (milliseconds). Can be raised as appropriate for individual slow operations (loading symbols, expanding children of large arrays, etc.)
configuration.codeblocks.keybindings.cbS: Enable Code::Blocks-faithful keybindings (off by default; all of them avoid the VS Code defaults): `F5` toggle breakpoint / `Shift+F8` stop debugging / `F2` open Build Log / `Ctrl+R` replace / `Ctrl+Shift+B` go to matching bracket / `Ctrl+Shift+C` comment / `Ctrl+Shift+S` save all / `Ctrl+Q` quit / `F12` collapse / `F7`·`Shift+F7`·`Ctrl+F7` step. Once enabled these keys override the VS Code defaults and are restored when it is turned off. Open the [visual keybinding settings panel](command:codeblocks.keybindings.panel) to fine-tune or unbind entries individually, or use [Check Keybinding Conflicts](command:codeblocks.keybindings.check) to see the conflict list.
configuration.codeblocks.keybindings.ove: Per-command custom keybindings (key = command short id, value = keybinding string, empty string = unbind). Changes are written to the user `keybindings.json` automatically (only managed entries are added/removed, plus `-command` rules for removed default keys; before the first write a backup is made as `keybindings.json.codeblocks-backup`). It is recommended to open the [visual keybinding settings panel](command:codeblocks.keybindings.panel) directly: press a key to record / type manually / unbind / restore defaults / export·import a scheme / reset all. Common key names: `build` / `rebuild` / `clean` / `run` / `buildAndRun` / `compileCurrentFile` / `debug` / `nextError` / `prevError` / `activatePriorProject` / `activateNextProject` / `moveProjectUp` / `moveProjectDown` / `projectTreeFocus` / `buildLogFocus`; CB-faithful group `cb*` (`cbToggleBreakpoint` / `cbBuildLog` / `cbReplace` / `cbStepOver` etc., 12 entries); external aliases `aliasGotoFile` / `aliasReplaceInFiles` / `aliasSelectNextMatch`. Example: `{ "build": "ctrl+alt+b", "cbQuit": "" }`
configuration.codeblocks.log.english.des: Output English text in the build log (summary/status messages aligned with the original Code::Blocks wording)
configuration.codeblocks.masterPath.desc: Compiler installation root directory (empty = detect from PATH)
configuration.codeblocks.maxReportedErro: Maximum number of errors collected per build (0 = unlimited). Aligned with Code::Blocks' max_reported_errors, preventing an excessive number of errors from slowing down the Build Log
configuration.codeblocks.parallelJobs.de: Number of parallel compile jobs (default 8; 0 = auto: logical cores × 2, capped at 32). Higher values speed up full builds but push CPU usage toward 100% and keep tens to hundreds of MB resident per compile process chain, so the default is kept at 8 to leave headroom for the editor and other extensions; specify a smaller value to save CPU/memory (1 = serial)
configuration.codeblocks.projectTree.cat: Group the project tree by file type (Sources / Headers / ASM Sources / Resources / Others, aligned with Code::Blocks). When off, files are shown by physical directory.
configuration.codeblocks.saveBeforeBuild: Automatically save unsaved files in the workspace before build/run/clean (aligned with Code::Blocks' Save all files before build)
configuration.codeblocks.todo.keywords.d: TODO keywords (scanned by the list command plus the type options of Add TODO Item; aligned with the CB todo plugin's keyword settings)
configuration.codeblocks.tools.markdownD: User-defined tools (aligned with Code::Blocks Tools → Configure tools…): listed at the end of the "Tools" menu and of the status bar menu, and run when selected. Supports the alias macros `${file}` / `${fileDir}` / `${projectDir}` / `${projectName}` / `${workspaceFolder}` and the Code::Blocks macros `$(VAR)` (such as `$(TARGET_OUTPUT_FILE)`, project custom variables `$(var)`). Example: `{ "name": "Disassemble", "command": "objdump", "arguments": "-d \"${file}\"", "output": "output" }`
configuration.codeblocks.ui.buildLogAuto: When to automatically focus the Build Log panel after a build finishes (aligned with Code::Blocks message_manager: by default it only acts on errors): errors = only when this build had errors (default); errorsAndWarnings = errors or warnings; always = always (the old behavior in 0.8.94 and earlier); never = never (it can still be opened from the menu/status bar)
configuration.codeblocks.ui.buildLogFocu: If errors exist when the build finishes, jump to the first error automatically (aligned with Code::Blocks' auto_focus_build_errors "Focus first error in the editor after build finishes", on by default); it is independent of buildLogAutoFocus, and F4 still steps through the errors when it is off
configuration.codeblocks.ui.findFileOpen: Also open the selected file when finding files (aligned with Code::Blocks' Find file → "Open file" checkbox; by default it only locates the file in this project tree)
configuration.codeblocks.ui.projectToolb: Buttons permanently shown in the title bar of the Project view (a button shown in the title bar no longer appears in the ⋯ overflow menu). Possible values: `newProject` / `openProject` / `build` / `rebuild` / `clean` / `run` / `debug` / `buildWorkspace` / `rebuildWorkspace` / `cleanWorkspace` / `compilerOptions` / `projectProperties` / `codeStats`
configuration.codeblocks.ui.quietFailure: Quiet mode for build failure: no failure toast, only log output plus the Build Log tree / status bar diagnostics badge
configuration.codeblocks.ui.quietSuccess: Quiet mode for build success: no success toast, only log output and the status bar diagnostics badge
configuration.codeblocks.ui.recentProjec: Maximum number of entries in the Recent Projects list (status bar menu; 0 = do not record)
Show the Symbols view (hidden by default initially, it can be brought up from ⋯ → Views in the view container; turning this setting off forces it hidden)
